title: KV index scrubbing and memory-channel allocator rescue for cross-tenant OOM cascades
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated experienced GPU OOM cascades during long-tail conversational sessions. Symptoms: abrupt worker process termination, KV index growth beyond expected bounds, and memory fragmentation that prevented allocator from reclaiming freed arenas. Root cause (preliminary): a race between prefix tombstone writes and the async KV index compaction path caused index metadata to accumulate stale slot references under certain session churn patterns; this in turn prevented the memory-channel allocator from coalescing adjacent freed regions, so large allocations for generation transiently failed and triggered OOMs.

Impact:
- Customer escalations opened (two P0s) for high-traffic hosted customers and a Dedicated customer running long-prompt pipelines.
- Observed across GPU-backed nodes and private clusters with heavy session churn (frequent session create/delete and long KV lifetimes).
- Some tenants saw repeated worker restarts; others experienced degraded tail latency due to repeated GC/eviction storms.

Goal:
- Ship a targeted runtime hotpatch that: 1) scrubs stale KV index entries proactively; 2) strengthens tombstone-to-compaction ordering to avoid index drift; 3) adds a temporary allocator backstop that temporarily widens the allocator coalescing window under pressure to avoid immediate OOMs.

Non-goal:
- This ticket does not include a full allocator rewrite or a heavyweight compaction redesign. Those are tracked separately and will follow after stabilization.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch deployed to canary pool without regressions (no increase in tail latency >5%)
KV index scrub runs and reduces stale index entries by >90% in affected workloads
Reproduce original OOM in a synthetic stress test before patch, and show OOM does not occur after patch under same load
Monitor dashboards show no new increase in GC/evict cycles and per-node memory usage stabilizes within 24 hours
Rollout plan documented and rollback tested
steps_taken: 2026-03-10 | Amira Patel | Triage call with SRE and on-call eng. Collected heap dumps, core traces and kv-index snapshots from hosted-region-1 and ddg-dedicated-03. Noticed index metadata growth correlates with session churn spike.

2026-03-11 | Diego Ramos | Reproduced memory growth in lab: synthetic session churn harness produced same stale-index pattern. Confirmed race between tombstone flush path and async compactor sweep (race window ~20-120s under churn).

2026-03-11 | Diego Ramos | Implemented prototype index-scrub task (passive, low-priority) that scans index slot sanity and drops unreachable slot refs; also added ordering fence in tombstone writer to ensure compactor sees consistent snapshot.
2026-03-12 | Priya Singh (SRE) | Applied prototype to internal staging fleet (canary 5 nodes). Observed immediate reduction in slot count and fewer mid-run evict storms. No regression in request P95.

2026-03-12 | Diego Ramos | Added allocator backstop: when fragmentation metric exceeds threshold, coalescer temporarily increases merge span to reclaim adjacent small regions proactively. Exposed config knobs for safety and telemetry.

2026-03-13 | QA (Lin) | Ran full synthetic heavy-churn test for 48 hours against canary. Pre-patch reproduced OOM within 6-12 hours; post-patch ran 48h with no OOM and stable GPU memory curve. Collected flamegraphs and allocator histograms.
2026-03-13 | Amira Patel | Drafted rollout playbook and incident communication for affected customers. Identified two Dedicated nodes with repeat occurrences; plan to remediate first then expand.

2026-03-14 | Diego Ramos | Opened PR with hotpatch and added feature flag `kv_index_scrub_v1` + allocator backstop flag. Tests added: unit for tombstone ordering, integration for scrub idempotency, stress harness for fragmentation behavior.
risks: Aggressive scrubbing could remove live but temporarily unreferenced slots if compactor ordering is incorrect — mitigated by conservative scrubbing window and idempotency checks
Allocator backstop temporarily widens coalescing window which could increase small-allocation latency — monitored via perf tests and feature-flag rollout
Hotpatch may interact with private on-prem installs where custom KMS/encryption adds latency to tombstone writes — will require slower canary cadence for Private customers
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to release branch behind feature flags
2) Deploy to internal staging and run 72h stress harness (already green on 48h)
3) Canary rollout: 5% of hosted GPU pool and 1 Dedicated customer node subset for 6h, monitor memory + evict cycles
4) If stable, expand to 25% and then 100% over 24h with automated rollback on OOM regression
5) Private clusters: offer opt-in patch and coordinate maintenance window with customers; require additional validation for on-prem hardware variants
postmortem_actions: Create follow-up epic for allocator redesign (link to ENG-505999 in backlog)
Add long-term compactor improvement story to reduce scrubbing need
Improve telemetry: expose per-tenant slot-age histogram and fragmentation heatmap
Customer comms: send targeted postmortem to affected accounts with mitigation timeline
